RunEvent.description:
Canonical event model for run updates.

`extra="ignore"`, not `"forbid"`. This model is not only constructed in
process - it is parsed back out of a Redis history that outlives any single
deployment (30-day TTL). Forbidding extras meant that *removing* a field
made every event already on disk unparseable: dropping the unused
`files_modified` / `tests_passed` / `tests_failed` counters took out the log
stream for every existing run at once, because `get_history` validates the
whole page and one bad record fails all of them.

Ignoring extras makes a field removal backward-compatible. A field
*addition* was always safe. Input still cannot invent fields the model
exposes, because unknown keys are dropped rather than kept.

SettingsUpdate.description:
Configuration an administrator may change at runtime.

Credentials are **write-only**. They can be set here because a self-hosted
endpoint that starts requiring a key is otherwise unfixable without a
redeploy, but nothing ever reads one back: responses carry a masked hint
only, the audit row records which credential changed and never its value,
and the stored copy is encrypted.

Three states per credential, which is what makes the form usable:
  omitted / null - leave whatever is stored alone
  ""             - delete the stored credential; the deployment's own
                   environment applies again
  a value        - set it

delivery_mode.description: fast: one sprint for a small product, files drafted from the specification, harness-run test rounds, building without reasoning. thorough: the full pipeline. Left out, the stored choice stands.

model_context_window.title: Model Context Window

model_max_output_tokens.description: The longest single reply, in tokens. 0 derives it from the context window (a quarter of it, capped). The reply and the conversation share one window, so raising this shrinks the conversation - every other budget is re-derived from what it leaves behind.

thinking_mode.description: 'default' sends nothing and leaves the model server's own setting in force; 'on' asks a reasoning-capable model to deliberate; 'off' explicitly disables it. 'off' is not the absence of 'on' - a server launched with reasoning enabled keeps it under 'default'.

StartRunRequest.description:
Request to start a run.

Credentials are deliberately absent. They used to be accepted here, which put
provider API keys into request bodies and access logs; the worker now
resolves them from its own environment or the secret store.

``artifact_directory`` is gone for the same class of reason: it named a
server path that became the repository root for every agent tool and the
sandbox bind mount, so a caller could point the whole run at any directory on
the host. A label is accepted instead, and the server derives the path.

delete.description:
Delete a terminal run and everything it owns.

Deletion cascades: uploads, workspace, checkpoints and event history all
go, and so do the transcript, ledger, journal and stored copies - see
`app.server.run_retention` for the full contract. Previously only the
metadata row was removed, so documents and checkpoints accumulated
forever - which is also a data-retention problem, not just a disk one.

get.description:
Download one artifact belonging to this run.

Two things changed here. The route is authenticated and tenant-scoped -
it previously sat on a router mounted with no auth dependency at all.
And the caller-supplied path is resolved *inside* the run's workspace and
rejected if it escapes; absolute paths used to be passed straight to
FileResponse, which made this an unauthenticated arbitrary file read.

post.description:
Create a new run from an existing run's documents.

The clone carries the source run's settings as well. Cloning exists so
an operator can repeat an attempt - for example after a run that died
in a way it cannot be resumed from - and it is only useful if the new
run behaves the same way: the same reviewer, the same review policy,
the same model choices, and the same attended/unattended mode.

Upload an existing codebase as an archive, for a brownfield run.

Stored, not yet extracted: it is unpacked into the workspace when the
run starts, so a run that is never started never expands an archive.

put.description:
Change non-secret provider settings for the whole system.

Stored in Postgres so every API worker and the Celery worker see one answer,
and so the change survives a restart. Writing to ``.env`` from a request
handler (the version before that) mutated a file the deployment also reads at
startup, which made runtime state and deployed configuration diverge.

post.description:
Measure the configured server's context window by asking it to refuse.

Admin-only and rate-limited by its own cost: it sends one deliberately
oversized request, which the server rejects before generating anything.

This exists because the window is the one setting that must be right and the
one nobody reliably knows. A model's advertised window is not what it was
loaded with - the same `gpt-oss-20b` serves 131,072 tokens or 8,192
depending on a slider - and no standard endpoint reports it. The refusal
does.
